method: Author self-score on the reviewer's rubric: silhouette and proportions 22/30, signature features 22/25, surface detail and material read 12/20, colour and value 13/15, readability at play distance 10/10. Judged from spring-hound.fidelity-compare.jpg (orthographic EEVEE renders of the low-poly model at the concept's side, front and back angles, framed at the concept's own metres per pixel: side 1.2 m / 855 px, front and back 1.21 m / 875 px) side by side, and from the six in-engine shots in staging/engine (shared brass sets with the manifest tint, hound-glow through the runtime D11 glow). glow-close is now its own frame: idle through a 30 degree lens aimed at the upper body, where idle uses the 50 degree seat lens. Changes since the 74 review: the head has a stop (the brow drops 34 mm between y 0.752 and 0.772) and the muzzle top and underside follow the concept profile within 1 to 5 mm from y 0.758 to 0.859, so the mouth closes to a 14 mm gap; the needle-teeth rows became three upper and two lower teeth per side plus a fang at the front (none reaches the jaw: at least 4.2 mm clearance through attack). The eyes are 54 by 32 mm almonds standing 12.7 mm proud of their dark sockets: in the engine idle shot the eye glow is 155 px against the grille's 543 px (0.29, concept 0.22, was 26 against 418). Skull and jaw moved to polished brass and both brass normal strengths from 0.35 to 0.18, so the head and chest no longer read as crumpled foil; engine idle head median #7D5D3D (V 0.49) beside the chest's 0.62. The chest is narrower head-on (cuirass half-width 0.126 to 0.128 m), the haunch's back edge is 4 cm further forward and the gaskin bulges forward (shin-to-haunch plate overlap down from 90 to 71 triangles at rest, 136 to 129 at worst in death). The winding key is one flat bow with two round lobes, 56 mm across with 24 mm holes and 105 mm between centres, centred on the key bone (centroid 0.2 mm off the spin axis), and the tail is ten chunky segments. Rubies are a deeper crimson (#A00048) on a gunmetal slot at roughness 0.25 and metallic 0.8: engine median #541920 to #661B29 (hue 349 to 353, S 0.70 to 0.76, V 0.33 to 0.40) against the concept's #680F23 (S 0.86, V 0.41); joints stay warm black (#25170E). Engine whole-body brass hue 24 to 31. The compare lighting is the fixed warden-matched rig and was not tuned to the score.
gaps: In the Blender front compare the polished skull mirrors the dark backdrop: head median V 0.16 against the concept's 0.63 (chest 0.69). The engine head reads lit (V 0.49). Putting only the skull back on aged brass measured compare V 0.29 but engine V 0.64, paler than the chest, so the skull stays polished.

The tail hangs to a key at z 0.45 m, where the concept's tail curls back up to a key at about 0.54 m; the head sits low on a forward neck rather than the concept's more upright one (both need bone moves).
Ruby saturation is still short of the concept: engine S 0.70 (idle), 0.76 (frozen), 0.74 (glow-close) against 0.86, and the rubies are seen mostly edge-on from the seat.

Glow hue is the project's amber (F08C2C): the engine grille and eyes are hue 33 to 42 against the concept's 25, and in the Blender compare the grille, lenses and eyes read peach at the GLOW_STRENGTH 0.7 convention.
From the seat camera the open jaw reads as a separate bar under the muzzle with the teeth showing; the concept shows a near-closed snarl.
Legs are still mostly plated cylinders below the forearm and gaskin; paws are simpler than the concept's arched, individually jointed toes, and the far-side legs are not staggered.
In the engine idle frame the chest prow's key-light highlight lifts the chest brass to V 0.62 (concept 0.45 to 0.53).
